title: Observation
description: Game state snapshot. Every section is optional; the SDK sends the sections OBSERVE asked for. Interest management: entity arrays are sorted by distance and cut to OBSERVE.max_n, legal_actions keeps the game's order and is cut to max_n too, and an observation that would exceed the text-frame cap (manifest limits.max_text_frame_bytes, default 262144) is truncated (entities by distance, legal_actions from the end) and flagged truncated: true.

legal_actions.description: The discrete moves the game would accept right now, in the game's order; perform one with CHOOSE. Ids are unique within the list. Sent only by engines whose manifest has supports.legal_actions. Never diffed: a STATE_UPDATE delta carries the whole list whenever it changed (an empty list when no move is legal) and leaves it out when it didn't.

state_flags.description: What the game itself is doing that holds the player, whether or not the scene has a player: a menu's intro dialogue, a loading screen. The standard holds are in_dialogue, cutscene, loading and paused; a game may add its own flags. A STATE_UPDATE delta never diffs the list: it carries the whole list whenever it changed ([] when no flag is set) and leaves it out when it didn't.

truncated.description: True when entities or legal actions were dropped to fit the text-frame cap.

max_health.description: Health at full. Lets the bot work out health / max_health.

state_flags.description: The player's own state (is_grounded, in_dialogue, ...). A hold the game reports whether or not there is a player goes in the observation's state_flags; an orchestrator reads both.

affordance.description: What the bot may do with it: interact (default), collect (a pickup to route through) or push (moved toward a plate, switch or ledge).

hazard.description: A danger to path around: static (spikes, lava) or moving (projectiles, with velocity). radius is in engine units.

type.description: What kind of control it is, one of the standard types: button (pressed to do something: a button, a menu entry, a link), checkbox (toggled on and off), option (a dropdown), slider (a number in a range, spin boxes included), text_input (a text field), label (text a player reads but can't operate), or control (any other control the game marks, such as a tab). Report the standard type, not the engine's class name (button, not Button or UButton).

text.description: The text a player reads on it. A button or checkbox reports its caption here even when the engine keeps it in a child text widget, and that child isn't reported as an element of its own. An option's text is its selected option, not its caption.

label.description: The name a player reads for the control, apart from what it shows (text) and holds (value): the caption beside a slider, a text field or a dropdown, such as Volume or Player name. It stays the same while the control is used. A button or checkbox usually has none, because its text names it.

visible.description: Whether it is on screen. An SDK may report a hidden or inactive control with visible false or leave it out; the two mean the same.

value.description: The control's current value: a slider's number, a checkbox's boolean, a text_input's text, an option's selected option. Absent or null for buttons, labels and controls.

ui_element.description: One control or piece of text in the game's UI. Every SDK reports the same thing for the same kind of control, so a locator means the same in every engine.

legal_action.description: One move the game would accept now.

id.description: Stable while the move stays legal; CHOOSE names it.

label.description: What a player sees, e.g. the card's name or the dialogue line.

targets.description: Entity ids the move can be aimed at. When present, CHOOSE must name one of them.

cost.description: Resource name → amount the move spends, e.g. {"energy": 1}.

group.description: Where the move comes from, e.g. hand or shop.

source.description: provider: listed by the game's legal-actions provider; ui: built from enabled visible UI controls.
